$comment: Cover-sheet spec only. The component inventory — ids, sections, groups, captions and variants — lives next to the @Previews as @CatalogGroup / @CatalogComponent / @CatalogVariant annotations under catalog/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/m3catalog/glimmer/, exactly as the sibling :catalog does. `referenceKits` names the Glimmer kit this sheet is compared against. Its "(Community)" suffix is the Figma Community channel Google publishes its kits through, not a third-party redraw — the Material 3 Design Kit this repository reproduces carries the same suffix — so `.design-parity.json`'s repo-wide `design-led` direction applies here unchanged. There is no `compareWith`: this sheet is rasterised by Robolectric while m3-catalog is rasterised by Skiko, so pairing the two would put a RENDERER difference into a comparison meant to be about design. `modes` is a single dark entry because Glimmer draws for an additive display where black is unlit — a light mode is not a thing the hardware can show — and the dark display surface keeps the preview server from staging these captures on white, which the additive-zero ground would vanish into. `display.hero` names the componentId `GlimmerLazyColumn/TwoLine`: the hero is the one picture the sheet leads with, and a column of real two-line ListItems fading into the additive black at its foot says more about Glimmer than any single control does. It also has the pixels for the front door's 196px well — 420x364 at this sheet's density, where a lone component sticker is ~141x48 and was stretched into a blur. It used to name the @Preview function `CardActionSticker`, which never resolved: that function publishes as a VARIANT of `Card` (preview id `card__ideal__default__content-action`), and the preview server resolves a hero against preview ids and componentId slugs, not function names, so the front door silently fell back to its own pick — the plain Button. A componentId is the one form both validate-catalog-spec and the server's lookup agree on.
